hero.headline: I build dependable software systems that make complex work feel simple.
hero.summary: This site is designed for recruiters and hiring teams to quickly understand how I think, what I build, and how consistently I ship. I will tailor the copy more specifically later, but the structure is ready for that story now.
hero.focus: DevOps, ML workflows, and Full-stack engineering
hero.asideTitle: A quick way to evaluate fit
hero.asideSummary: Instead of just listing tools, this portfolio pairs project highlights with a GitHub activity dashboard so you can see both the results and the operating habits behind them.

projects.title: Projects that show how I build
projects.intro: A focused selection of projects that reflects the systems, tooling, and product work I enjoy building.

descriptions.Market-Regime-Detection-With-Auto-Model-: An end-to-end, local-first MLOps pipeline that detects market regimes and automatically switches among specialized models.
descriptions.AWS-Dashboard: A full-stack AWS cost-visibility dashboard with workspace access, authenticated collaboration, billing analysis, and cloud-ready deployment.
descriptions.ACC-MLOps-Project: A collaborative machine-learning application combining a Python/FastAPI backend, web frontend, model artifacts, and team delivery workflows.

projects.emptyState: Add repository names to site/data/content.json or configure the GitHub token to populate these project cards automatically.

github.title: A live view of how I work in 2026
github.intro: The goal here is not vanity metrics. It is to show consistency, code review participation, and the shape of my output over time in a recruiter-friendly format.
github.heatmapHelper: Keyboard focus and hover both reveal daily counts.
github.callout: This panel highlights rhythm rather than just totals, which helps frame how steadily I contribute across the year.
github.activityEmptyState: Recent pull requests, issues, commits, and reviews will appear here once GitHub data is available.
github.readingSummary: Commit counts alone rarely tell the full story, so this section also surfaces pull requests, issues, and reviews to better represent collaboration and delivery.
